sources.note: Fresh independent read on 2026-11-26 at agent-5 snapshot 1a908eac; item, mapping, plan and layout are byte-identical to 4aae1ccd, where my earlier record stood. All 21 go, uncut, to the Persian field of r00001-sf8ca119bc7deb30b at offsets 0-20; moving Persian out of the Arabic slot is right. Kind heading: I agree, and this closes my open kind finding. Grounds: (1) the row is what marks the start of numbered section 20, and it names the source; it tells the reader nothing to do, so by itself it is not an instruction; the direction to the reader is wholly in r00002, which is instruction and ends with a colon. (2) The source itself puts these words in a row of their own; the split keeps that row and does not move the break. (3) Keeping the kind keeps the published ID r00001-sf8ca119bc7deb30b live, so no link changes. One thing I record so that it is not lost: grammatically the name is the subject of the verb that opens r00002, so one sentence runs from this heading into the next row. That is a property of the source's row break. It is not a fault of the split and not a reason to change the kind; I name it only for a later editorial pass. The coordinator decided on 2026-11-26 to keep heading; I checked the row again before recording this and I agree with the decision on my own reading.
